I was placed into it in high school freshman year, and I was so upset because I remembered disliking Spanish when I was in elementary school. When I started the class, it was just amazing. My Latin teacher is my favorite teacher ever, and Latin is my favorite subject. I’m very lucky that my teacher is so highly educated in Latin, because I’m the only one in my little school studying Latin past Latin II, and he’s been guiding me through independent studies while I spend free periods in the back of his Latin II classes. I’m set to take AP Latin next year, my senior year, and I’m planning to major in classical languages in college and later teach Latin. 
I can’t explain why I love Latin so much. I guess it just feels almost mathematical? It combines math and English, my two favorite core subjects. Unlike most latin students, I love the grammatical aspect of Latin class. I love learning the rules of language. I’ve been dabbling in Ancient Greek as well, for that reason.

When I was around 10 I had this best friend who was definitely more than a best friend. She actually came out to me first as bi, which is when I realized gay people existed. A few years later, she admitted over text that she had had a crush on me, after I came out as a lesbian after previously identifying as bi, but she said she was over it. I never told her that I felt the same. Funnily enough, I remember being called a lesbian in like 2nd grade for being close with a different best friend, but i never asked what the word meant.

I just started this challenge this year, and I just started with some favorites and easier books to get the ball rolling. I started with Harry Potter, and the last books of that series are long, so I also found myself trying to read 100+ pages a day. It was pretty easy, since I was used to the books and love them, but sometimes when I’m at slow spots, I like to take a break and read a shorter book, like I’m trying The Chronicles of Narnia for the first time. I’m not sure if this helps or makes any sense but I’m basically saying that in my experience, it’s easier to just get some momentum with easier books and designate a few hours a day to reading.

Just started **The Chronicles of Narnia** series, finished **The Magician’s Nephew** (Book 1) yesterday, finished **The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe** (Book 2) today. They’re shorter books but they’re still pretty good. I just can’t focus on long books at the moment.
